# Hand Extensor Tendon Lacerations

**Authors:** Bryan G. Beutel, Kristof S. Gutowski, Raghavendra Marappa-Ganeshan

**Source:** StatPearls - StatPearls Publishing

## Abstract

Extensor tendon lacerations of the hand are relatively common injuries that, when not treated appropriately, may lead to a lasting impairment of hand function. These lacerations often result in an extensor lag that can predispose the affected digit(s) to further injury and interfere with the performance of myriad activities. Due to their superficial location with minimal overlying soft tissue coverage and proximity to underlying osseous structures, hand extensor tendons are more prone to injury than flexor tendons. The primary management goal of these injuries is to restore both tendon continuity and digital function, while a secondary goal is to permit early motion of the affected digit.
